MotionPoint.description:
Measured and predicted position of the object in one epoch stack, as offsets from
the first epoch where it was measured. Offsets in arcseconds; east is positive.

error_east_arcsec.description: 1-sigma uncertainty of the measured offset (both visits combined); null for the first visit, whose offset is zero by definition
error_east_arcsec.title: Error East Arcsec

error_method.description: `bootstrap`: spread of the fitted position when the visit is re-stacked from its exposures drawn with replacement; `fit`: the fit's own covariance (too few bootstrap fits)
error_method.title: Error Method

measured_east_arcsec.description: Gaussian fit in the object-centred stack of this visit. Null when too faint to measure
measured_east_arcsec.title: Measured East Arcsec

parallax_east_arcsec.description: The part of the predicted offset that is parallax (0 without `parallax`)
parallax_east_arcsec.title: Parallax East Arcsec

predicted_east_arcsec.description: Proper motion plus parallax (when `parallax` is given)
predicted_east_arcsec.title: Predicted East Arcsec

saturated.description: The object's core is flagged in this visit (a saturated star): no S/N, and the position is fitted to the wings, so its error is statistical only
saturated.title: Saturated

snr.description: S/N at the predicted position in the object-centred stack of this visit
snr.title: Snr

get.description: Is the service up, and is it serving real or synthetic data?

Quick-look brightness at a point in every exposure: plot against wavelength for a
spectrum, or against time for a light curve.

For a moving object, give its proper motion: each exposure is measured where the object
was on that date. Points whose aperture holds flagged or missing pixels have a null
`flux`. A first request for a position can take about a minute in live mode; then it
is cached.

get.description: Name to coordinates. Knows only the built-in test targets for now.

Many exposures added together, so that faint objects appear.

Uses every exposure in the wavelength range (up to the server's stack cap, not the
blink player's cap). Returns one typical single exposure, the `tracked` stack (each
exposure centred on the object's predicted position), the `static` stack (one fixed
sky grid; null without proper motion), one stack per visit (`epochs`, same fixed
grid), and the object's measured and predicted motion between visits. A first
request for a position can take about a minute in live mode; then it is cached.
